title: Error Variant Garden — request clustering + payload diff dashboard
creator: Maya Chen
description: Design a composable dashboard for console users that surfaces 'error variants' — clustered groups of failed requests that share root causes — with an emphasis on rapid triage: aggregated timelines, atomic payload diffs, retry lineage, rollout overlays, and cost-of-failure estimates. The goal is to let engineers and SREs move from signal to fix in under 10 minutes for common classes of infra and model-related failures.
rationale: Existing console views show failed requests as lists or single-request traces. Teams need a middle layer that groups similar failures and makes subtle payload differences visible, highlights how rollouts or model swaps changed the distribution, and ties failures to cost and retry behavior. This reduces noise and surfaces actionable hypotheses for remediation.
user_stories: As an SRE I want to see clusters of similar errors so I can prioritize incidents by impact and recurrence.
As an ML engineer I want payload diffs and model input histograms so I can detect regressions tied to prompt shapes.
As a PM I want rollout overlays so I can correlate feature flag or model rollouts with spikes in a variant.
As a support engineer I want quick links to retry traces and canonical examples to reproduce customer issues.
As an engineering manager I want cost-per-variant estimates to prioritize fixes that reduce spend or customer-facing failures.
acceptance_criteria: Prototype in Figma with at least three canvas states: overview (variant garden), variant detail (payload diff + timeline), and incident correlation panel (rollout + cost overlays).
Clickable prototype that demonstrates selecting a cluster and surfacing three representative requests (canonical, median, outlier).
Payload diff view that highlights key-value deltas and shows field-level prevalence across the cluster.
Rollout overlay that can layer a time-series of deployment events (model-version, region, routing policy) against variant frequency.
Design tokens and component list documented in the ticket for front-end implementation handoff.
ux_notes: Use 'garden' metaphor: clusters represented as nodes sized by request volume and colored by error class (timeout, model-error, quota, predicate).
Allow switching clustering granularity (coarse, standard, fine) with a slider; default to 'standard' derived from heuristic combining error signature + payload fingerprint.
Provide 'canonical request' selection automated by least-latency and most-complete response; allow manual pinning.
Include a sparse KV-diff widget that collapses low-signal fields and surfaces high-entropy fields first.
Ensure all charts respect user-selected time ranges and preserve selection across drilldowns.
decisions: Cluster identity will be computed server-side by the diagnostics pipeline and surfaced via an aggregate endpoint; the UI will not re-cluster client-side.
Payload diffs will be shown as line-by-line key comparisons and a compact field-frequency histogram to indicate prevalence.
Color palette chosen to prioritize accessibility (WCAG AA) and to reuse existing console semantic colors for error severity.
We will surface cost estimates using existing token-cost aggregation without introducing new billing semantics.
tradeoffs: Server-side clustering reduces client complexity but adds dependency on diagnostics infra and may delay rolling out the UI without backend readiness.
Showing representative canonical requests speeds triage but risks biasing users toward a single example; mitigated by exposing median and outlier picks.
Adding rollout overlays increases cognitive load; we mitigate by defaulting overlays off and surfacing them on hover or via a 'correlate' toggle.
open_questions: What heuristic threshold should determine when to collapse variants into 'other' to avoid over-segmentation?
Should we allow users to define custom clustering rules (e.g., ignore session_id, client_time) or is that an advanced follow-up?
Do we need a write-back action for reviewers to mark a variant as 'triaged' or 'known-issue' and sync to incident tracker?
How will this UI behave for extremely high-cardinality payloads (base64 blobs, attachments)?
implementation_notes: Frontend should reuse the console's mini-chart and timeline components to maintain consistency.
Introduce a new 'variant-id' field in the diagnostics API to avoid expensive fingerprint recomputation in the UI.
Plan for progressive enhancement: show basic cluster metadata immediately and lazy-load payload diffs when a variant is expanded.
Include instrumentation events for: variant_open, canonical_switch, payload_diff_expand, correlate_with_rollout.
review_feedback: PM (Ibrahim Khan): Good direction; emphasize cost overlay use cases for internal stakeholders and include a short tooltip describing estimate methodology.
Eng (Priya Nair): Backend contract looks fine; ask infra to support low-latency sampling for canonical picks to keep UI snappy.
Security (Evan Liao): Make sure PII-scrubbing rules are surfaced and that sample requests default to masked mode in the UI.
Design lead (Ana Martinez): Consider micro-interactions when collapsing/expanding nodes to maintain context; add microcopy for 'why these requests are grouped'.

notes_for_engineering: Please implement server-side endpoints that return: cluster metadata (variant_id, label, volume, error_types), three representative requests, prevalence map for fields, and a time-series for variant frequency.
Prefer streaming or chunked responses for payload diffs for very large clusters to avoid UI timeouts.
Add feature flag 'variantGarden' to gate the rollout and allow performance experiments.
